//: MOBILE. The desktop config is the sibling file; this one exists because
CLAUDE.md says a working mobile experience is not optional, and nothing was
measuring it. There is no preset here on purpose — mobile is what Lighthouse
does by default: 412x823, simulated slow 4G, and a 4x CPU slowdown on top of
everything that already costs this site its desktop score.
The floor was left out until there was a measurement. The first successful
run — CI #8, 27 August 2026 — produced:
performance 38    accessibility 96    best practices 96    SEO 100
FCP 1.0s          LCP 7.1s            CLS 0.014           TBT 146,790ms
So the floor is 0.35, three points under the measurement, and it is a
ratchet: it goes up when the number goes up and never comes down to make a
run green. 38 is a bad score and writing it down is the point.
It took three attempts to get this number at all. The first run used a
'mobile' preset that does not exist. The second and third collected and
asserted correctly and then died uploading, because both Lighthouse runs in
the job wrote their artifact under the same name. The measurement is the
easy part; getting it out of the job was not.
LCP is asserted loosely at 9s. It measured 7.1 and the runner is shared and
noisy, so a tight bound would fail for reasons that have nothing to do with
the site. It is here so that a better performance score cannot be bought by
making the page paint later.
//upload: There is deliberately no `upload` block. There was one, pointing at
./.lighthouseci-mobile, and it never did anything: the GitHub action
hardcodes its results directory to $PWD/.lighthouseci and runs its own
config at all. So the setting looked like configuration and was inert,
and the CI step that archived ./.lighthouseci-mobile archived nothing
while reporting a warning nobody read. Uploading is the action's job;
